headline: Sunday's the clean window, but the break has slid off
body:
Patchy dense fog both mornings, visibility a mile or less — run slow out of the harbor. Sunday is the day to be out: channel seas 2 ft, the triangle running about 2.7, winds light NW 5 to 10 all day. Monday turns on you — the triangle goes 13 kn gusting 16 by afternoon, and the western and outer grounds fare worse: Santa Rosa building from 14 to 19 gusting 21, San Nicolas 12 gusting 14 early. If you fish, fish Sunday.

The trouble is temperature. The whole chart reads 71–73 °F — nothing on the cool side of the 64–68 band anywhere in the data. Inside the triangle the west corner off Santa Cruz is coolest at 72, the south point 72.5, the east off Anacapa 72.9; if you must start, work that west edge. But the break isn't in the triangle at all, and it hasn't set up on the farther grounds either — the coolest water, Santa Rosa Flats and San Nicolas at 71.2, still sits above the band. Not a textbook bluefin day.
